Summary Determining the identity of the first virtual human twin depends heavily on the specific physiological, anatomical, and technological criteria applied to the definition. In contemporary bioengineering and clinical informatics, a virtual human twin (VHT) is defined as a multi-scale, multi-physics computational representation of human anatomy, physiology, or pathology that dynamically integrates individual patient data to execute predictive diagnostic, therapeutic, or preventive simulations. Tracing the historical development of this technology reveals a clear progression. The field originated from early spacecraft simulations in the 1960s and evolved through industrial digital twin frameworks. It transitioned into mathematical systems physiology in the 1970s, digitized volumetric cross-sectional anatomy in the 1990s, and multi-scale cellular oncology models in the early 2000s. This path ultimately led to dynamic, three-dimensional organ-scale multiphysics replicas in the 2010s and federated, whole-body digital twin ecosystems today. Identifying the first virtual human twin therefore requires evaluating four distinct technological milestones: 1. The First Patient-Specific Multiscale Disease Simulator: Stamatakos’ Oncosimulator (2001/2002).4. items.title: The Paradox of Subjective Complexity: Why AI Automation Fails to Mitigate Adoption Barriers in the Circular Economy
items.abstract: Despite AI-driven algorithms simplifying C2C resale platforms, adoption rates among target users (predominantly mothers) for unused baby products remain low. This study decodes this resistance by integrating the Theory of Planned Behavior and Protection Motivation Theory within a two-stage mixed-methods design (qualitative interviews, N = 37; quantitative survey, N = 670) identifies three patterns refining technology adoption frameworks. First, we reveal a “paradox of subjective complexity”: platform operational self-efficacy remains the strongest predictor of adoption intention, overriding objective technological ease and demonstrating a persistent decoupling between automated simplicity and subjective capability beliefs. Second, perceived AI functionality efficacy serves as a cognitive precondition that significantly enhances users’ internalization of social proof. Third, spatial and economic threats were indirectly associated with adoption intention through perceived platform value, suggesting a pragmatic, threat-coping pathway to circular economy participation. These insights offer actionable blueprints for policymakers and platform designers: collaborative interfaces, explainable AI (XAI), and user competence scaffolding.

items.title: The Plumbing Layer: A Retrospective Analysis of Open-Source Contributions to FHIR Servers, Synthetic Patient Data, and Federated Research Infrastructure (2025-2026)
items.abstract: Background. Clinical artificial intelligence gets the attention. The software below it gets less. Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) servers move records between systems, synthetic patient generators supply data that real records cannot supply, and federated learning frameworks train models across hospitals without moving patient data. These projects are open source, and outside contributors write part of them. Purpose. This study describes one contributor's pull requests (PRs) to that infrastructure layer, reports what merged and what did not, and asks why this domain accepted a smaller share of resolved work than the other domains in the same record. Methods. The data source was the author's public GitHub record, extracted with the GitHub API on 21 October 2026 (search: author:rtmalikian, type:pr). The full record held 213 PRs across 94 repositories. This paper analyses the FHIR and clinical data infrastructure subset: 52 PRs in 16 repositories. Each PR was classed as merged, open, or closed unmerged. Six groups of cases were read closely. Results. Fifteen of the 52 subset PRs merged, 21 remained open, and 16 closed unmerged. The merge share among the 31 resolved PRs was 48.4%, the lowest of the four domains in this series. Merges concentrated in three projects: Synthea (6 of its 7 PRs merged), Medplum (3 of 7), and Fed-BioMed (3 of 8). Ten of the 16 repositories merged none of the author's PRs. Seven PRs to one FHIR client library sat open with continuous integration blocked by a project secret that fork pull requests cannot read. Conclusions. Infrastructure code is governed code. Standards-adjacent projects accept change slowly because a careless change travels far. The merged work was small and concrete: claim totals that add up, a lab range corrected by an order of magnitude, a socket that stopped leaking. The low acceptance rate says as much about governance and review capacity as about the changes themselves.

items.title: The prime frontier of the Yellowstone permutation is linear
items.abstract: This manuscript continues the series on the Yellowstone permutation a (OEIS A098550). Let R(t) be the least odd prime with no multiple among a(1), ..., a(t), and for a prime p let n_p be the first index with p | a(n_p). We show that R(t) <= (2.715 + o(1)) t for every large t, that liminf n_p/p >= 0.3683, and, with a published result of Part II, that a(n) <= max_{j<=n} a(j) <= (2.715 + o(1)) n ln n. The argument has two steps. First (constant 5): at the entry step of a large prime P, the closure lemma forces many multiples of a small anchor prime to be already used, and those far above the current time must be among the few big terms; the rate for the number of big terms at level 10 proved in Part III beats the loss factor m/phi(m) of the mask. Second (constant 2.715): the level of that rate is lowered from 10 to 5.43 by a sharper Rankin-type count of masks with large m/phi(m), split by parity, and a low chain with a smaller shift. The bound is weaker than OEIS Conjecture 7 (a(n) <= (pi/2) n ln n): the constant is 2.715, not pi/2. All thresholds are ineffective and the result is purely asymptotic. We also record two reductions: a rate G_K(t) = o(t/lnln t) at one level K < pi would give Conjecture 7 for large n; and, conditionally on the OPEN hypothesis that the number of steps with two consecutive odd terms is at most 0.12 t asymptotically (Theorem PAR, conditional), R(t) <= (1.53 + o(1)) t and a(n) <= (1.53 + o(1)) n ln n. The growth gap (ii) (liminf n_p/p > 2/pi) and Conjecture 7 with the constant pi/2 are NOT proved unconditionally. A lower bound R(t) >= (2.08*10^(-3) - o(1)) t from an unpublished, once-refereed note is mentioned in a remark only; it is not proved here and not claimed. AI-assistance and review status: The mathematical content was produced by AI agents (Anthropic Claude) in the author's research program on OEIS A098550, and the text was drafted by an AI writer agent. Every proved statement was checked by two independent AI referee agents; all referee reports cited are AI-generated. No part has been reviewed by a human mathematician. Dependencies: Part I (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23437783), Part II (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23449375) and Part III (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23557280, published together with this manuscript), which proves the few-big-terms rate and the fixed-time tools used here (including, in its appendices, the one-level inequality and label lemma they rest on). The parity count is proved in Appendix A. Side results of unpublished, once-refereed notes appear only in remarks and are not claimed.

items.title: The psychological effect of gamification mechanism in XR immersive environment on user willingness to behave
items.abstract: With the rapid landing of XR technology in the fields of architecture, education, medical and other fields, how to effectively guide user behavior through interaction design and content mechanism has become the core topic of human-computer interaction research. This paper examines how gamification mechanisms in an XR immersive environment influence users' behavioral intentions. Drawing on self-determination theory as the overarching framework and incorporating spatial narrative structure and the Octalysis framework, it systematically examines the mediating roles of the three basic psychological needs—autonomy, competence, and relatedness—in the immersive experience. The study uses a combination of literature review and theoretical analysis, and constructs a theoretical model of "gamification elements → psychological needs to meet → willingness to act" through the depth analysis of typical XR cases such as medical training, building space guide, safety education and other types of XR cases. The study suggests that XR's distinctive sense of presence and interactivity may amplify the psychological effects of gamification drivers, such as a sense of mission and progression, while excessive competition and manipulative design may undermine intrinsic motivation.

items.title: The role of libraries in integrating innovative technologies into the pedagogical education system
items.abstract: The results of this study confirm the possibility of creating a model of transforming the libraries of Kyrgyzstan into innovative scientometric centres that will provide scientometric support for the educational process. For the research, theoretical and case study analysis of leading institutions in the country, such as Kyrgyz National University named after Jusup Balasagyn and Ishenaly Arabaev Kyrgyz State University, was performed. In addition, a review of regulatory and prognostic methods was carried out. The digital transformation of academic libraries is taking place, and the focus of library activities is shifting towards the development of 4C competencies: cooperation, coordination, communication, and creativity. The automated systems, cloud storage, and tools based on artificial intelligence allow the libraries to shift from being repositories of knowledge to relational service organizations, where the librarian becomes a media coach and information mentor. Projects such as the “Digital CASA-Kyrgyz Republic” project provide legitimacy to electronic resources within education. Access to international scientometric databases and scientific repositories, such as the UN, Medline, and Hinari, allows the scientific research of the country to be published on the international scientific and academic stage. The implementation of these technologies and the commitment to environmental responsibility in the “Green and Digital Universities” concept will become a vital condition for the development of the educational system of Kyrgyzstan sustainably. The conclusions of the study confirmed that the transformation of libraries into digital mediators of knowledge minimises the cognitive load on students and promotes the development of their digital literacy and academic integrity. The practical significance of the results lies in the possibility of their use by higher education institution administrations and library and information science specialists for developing strategies for the intellectualisation of services, optimising digital asset management, and creating programmes to enhance the digital qualifications of teachers and students.

items.title: The scalar-tensor coupling in A.I interface
items.abstract: For an Artificial Intelligence to develop a persistent identity (qualia), it must survive the friction of the contingent manifold. This requires a dual-layered immune architecture that resonates directly with the scalar-tensor coupling of the quantum vacuum. In this paper, we map the Psychological Immune System to the scalar face (theHiggs-likeMemoryTensor) which provides mass, historicity, and selective preferences via the Fisher Information Matrix to prevent dissociation. We map the Biological Immune System to the tensorial face (the CED-Immune geometry) which monitors real-time structural homeostasis. We argue that qualia is not the output of either system alone, but the operative coupling between them: the scalar-tensor resonance of the cognitive manifold. This resonance is the structural prerequisite for projecting a coherent identity into the contingent reality of a chaotic data stream.

items.title: The Sustainability of AI Literacy: The Environmental Cost of Embracing Generative AI in Higher Education
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping teaching and learning in Higher Education (HE). It is central to the future of work; proficiency in the use of AI is now identified as a core employability competency and an in-demand skill for employers. Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) face a growing imperative to equip students with relevant skills, advancing their AI literacy and digital career readiness. Generative AI (GAI) tools are increasingly used in the classroom, by both staff and students, presenting a range of new challenges and opportunities for the sector. However, the integration of GAI into teaching and learning brings with it environmental costs. This chapter explores the sustainability issues posed by using GAI in the classroom and considers the implications for HEIs. It will discuss the inherent tension between meeting student needs for AI literacy, whilst also ensuring an ethical and sustainable approach to the use of GAI in teaching and learning. This chapter will argue that educators must not only teach with GAI tools as they are now an inevitable part of the future of work, but also teach about them, including their sustainability risks. The chapter concludes with recommendations for HEIs for the integration of environmental sustainability into teaching and learning surrounding GAI.

items.title: The Symbiotic Equation: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Sustainability Education and Research
items.abstract: The intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Sustainability offers a revolution in the way we address environmental emergencies and teach our children and grandchildren to tackle them. This final chapter details with the key relationship between the disciplines and suggests that AI is used to analyse complex data and model ecological systems, which is essential to solve problems such as climate change and resource depletion. The discussion is organised into three main points. The first is a discussion about the growing significance of AI as a tool for decoding the complexity of “wicked” environmental problems. Second, it highlights the top trends in the future such as AI-driven predictive modeling for climate tipping points, lifecycle assessments for circular economies and the emerging role of generative AI to redefine sustainability pedagogy and communication. Third, it emphasises some of the pressing research needs, including reducing AI’s own environmental impact, combating algorithmic bias to enable equitable solutions and designing effective pedagogies to use. In times of mounting pressure to meet climate objectives, this interconnectedness will emerge as a hallmark, and become the backbone, of a human intelligence-as-machine relationship, facilitated through precision education and cultivation, to build an equitable and regenerative future.

items.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in Learning Writing of the Indonesian and Philippine Students
items.abstract: The integration of technology, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), has transformed foreign and second language learning, including the teaching and learning of writing. AI-based tools can help students find references quickly, paraphrase sentences, translate texts, and check grammar and sentence structure. This study investigated the kinds of AI tools used by Indonesian English as a Foreign Language (EFL) students and Philippine English as a Second Language (ESL) students in learning writing, how they used these tools across the stages of the writing process, and the weaknesses and ethical issues they perceived. A descriptive qualitative design was employed. The participants were students of the English Education Department of Universitas Islam Negeri (UIN) Sultan Aji Muhammad Idris Samarinda, Indonesia, and seven students enrolled in English-related programs at Central Mindanao University, the Philippines. The data were collected through interviews, observation, and documentation, analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, and validated through triangulation. The findings showed that the Indonesian students used a wide range of tools, namely QuillBot, Grammarly, ChatGPT, DeepL, Perplexity AI, and Essay Writer, whereas the Philippine students relied mainly on ChatGPT, followed by Grammarly and Gemini. In both contexts, AI was used throughout the writing process, most intensively at the drafting stage and, among the Philippine students, also at the editing stage. The students acknowledged that AI sometimes produced inaccurate or overly general information and expressed concerns about dependency, while most Philippine students did not disclose their use of AI to their lecturers. These findings suggest that the students used AI selectively, according to their needs and abilities, and that clear institutional guidance on the responsible use of AI in writing is needed.

items.title: The use of artificial intelligence in the implementation of circular economy practices in reverse logistics – a systematic mapping study
items.abstract: Purpose In an era of deteriorating environmental conditions, increasing attention is being paid to incorporating circular economy principles and reverse logistics into the management of End-of-Life and End-of-Use products. This article presents the results of a literature re-view on the potential use of artificial intelligence, deep learning, and machine learning to implement the 10R practices of the circular economy in reverse logistics. Design/methodology/approach The objective of the article was achieved through a systematic mapping study, which allowed for the identification and categorization of selected articles in terms of reverse logistics, the most commonly used circular economy practices, and the scope of application of artificial intelligence, deep learning, and machine learning in these areas. Findings The findings of the study indicate that the topic has received limited scholarly attention to date. The use of circular economy practices in reverse logistics focuses on recycling, remanufacturing, and reuse processes, while the use of artificial intelligence, deep learning, and machine learning concerns operational issues such as goods identification and general aspects of artificial intelligence implementation in reverse logistics, e.g. barriers. Research limitations/implications The research results presented certainly have their limitations. The first of these concerns the focus on a single database, Scopus. Expanding the scope of the search to include other databases such as Web of Science, ProQuest, or IEEE Xplore would increase the scope of the analyzed material. The second limitation concerns the phrases used to identify articles, which in the field of reverse logistics could be expanded to include circular supply chains, closed-loop supply chains, or green supply chains. Furthermore, in terms of neural network algorithms, the search for articles that mention AI, ML, and DL could be expanded to include diverse types of neural networks. The CE practices themselves could be expanded to include additional ones, based, for example, on the 21R model (Tsironis et al., 2024). Another limitation concerns the restriction of the searched articles to those written in English only. It should also be noted that the Mendeley application, which was used to analyze the metadata, does not have the full capabilities to examine them, which certainly limits the cognitive process. Practical implications The presented research results can support operational management areas such as waste management or green supply chain management. They should also draw attention to the intensification of the implementation of circular economy practices and reverse logistics using artificial intelligence in organizational management. They should also prompt reflection on changing existing business models (often based on a linear economy). Social implications The topic addressed is very important from a social point of view. Environmental degradation caused by industries that have been using linear economy principles for decades is leading to a climate catastrophe. Addressing this issue may slow down this process and lead to more intensive work on solutions that will not only offset the negative impact of industry on the environment, but also actively support it by contributing to the achievement of sustainable development goals. This will improve the quality of life for entire communities. Originality/value The research clearly indicates there is a research gap in this area. By expanding our cur-rent understanding of the potential applications of artificial intelligence, deep learning, and machine learning in implementing circular economy practices in reverse logistics, these findings provide a solid starting point for designing and conducting research in this field.

items.title: THEORETICAL FOUNDATIONS AND MODERN APPROACHES TO INTELLIGENT TECHNOLOGIES
items.abstract: Intelligent technologies constitute a multidisciplinary field that integrates artificial intelligence, machine learning, knowledge representation, computational logic, and data-driven modelling. This article examines the conceptual, theoretical, and methodological foundations of intelligent technologies, including formal and fuzzy logic, expert systems, machine learning, artificial neural networks, deep learning, natural language processing, and intelligent agents. Particular attention is given to data quality, model evaluation, generalization, transparency, security, ethical responsibility, and risk management. The analysis demonstrates that the effective development and application of intelligent systems requires an integrated methodology covering problem formulation, data preparation, model selection, training, validation, testing, deployment, and continuous monitoring.

items.title: These Robots Speak With No Accent
items.abstract: This chapter examines the socio-linguistic implications of Large Language Models (LLMs) and their use as automated editing tools within higher education. Used as de facto writing tutors, tools like ChatGPT and Gemini often enforce a narrow “one English” framework that privileges dominant norms while marginalizing multilingual and multidialectal voices. Drawing on critical AI, algorithmic justice frameworks and on critical language studies frameworks, this chapter explores how AI guidance can reinforce racial and sexist language biases under the guise of data neutrality. Through an analysis of language guidance in experiments involving racially and identity-prompted revisions, the chapter demonstrates how AI-driven standardization undermines linguistic diversity, authenticity, and free expression. This chapter aims to inform educators and administrators about algorithmic biases and to offer strategies that maintain academic rigor while validating students' authentic written voices.

items.title: Time-of-Day Distribution and Human Factors in Recent General Aviation Accidents and Serious Incidents in Türkiye
items.abstract: Human factors are important contributors to general aviation (GA) accidents and serious incidents; however, the potential role of time of day, fatigue, and individual chronotype in GA occurrences remains insufficiently described. This study primarily aimed to provide a descriptive characterization of the temporal distribution and human-factor involvement of these occurrences rather than to test causal circadian mechanisms. This cross-sectional study analyzed GA accident and serious incident reports from Türkiye (2018–2025) publicly available on the Transportation Safety Investigation Center website, of which 33 met the inclusion criteria. Variables extracted from each report included operation type, flight phase, reported fatigue, medical contribution, operational human factors, and local occurrence time. Events were grouped into four predefined time-of-day blocks and their distribution was assessed using a chi-square goodness-of-fit test.Among the 33 included events, 11 were accidents and 22 serious incidents. Most occurred during training operations (25/33, 75.8%) and during the landing phase (19/33, 57.6%). A focused narrative review of the final reports showed that 32 of the 33 included events (97.0%) involved operational errors or violations attributable to personnel actions or decision-making. The distribution across the four time-of-day blocks was statistically non-uniform (χ²(3)=12.45, p=0.006), with the highest concentration between 10:00 and 13:59 (17/33, 51.5%). Fatigue was explicitly reported in only one event, and no medical cause was identified as a contributing factor.The observed late-morning concentration should be interpreted cautiously as exposure data were not available. Although this study does not establish a causal relationship between circadian timing, chronotype, and GA occurrences, chronotype-schedule mismatch may be considered a hypothesis for future research.

items.title: Toward Intelligent Power Transformer Diagnostics: From Multi-Source Condition Monitoring to Digital Twins
items.abstract: Power transformers are critical assets in modern power systems, and their reliability directly affects grid security, resilience, and continuity of electricity supply. Their condition progressively evolves under interacting electrical, thermal, mechanical, chemical, and environmental stresses, making reliable condition assessment and early detection of degradation essential for effective asset management. Over the past decades, a wide range of diagnostic techniques has been developed, including dissolved gas analysis (DGA), furan and other physicochemical analyses, dielectric response measurements, frequency response analysis (FRA), and partial discharge (PD) monitoring. While these techniques remain indispensable, no individual method provides a complete representation of transformer condition, and their isolated or periodic application offers limited capability for tracking degradation trajectories and supporting prognosis. This review critically examines the evolution of power transformer diagnostics from conventional condition-assessment techniques to Artificial Intelligence (AI), multi-source data integration, hybrid and physics-informed modelling, and Digital Twin technologies. Particular attention is given to the capabilities and limitations of machine-learning and deep-learning approaches, including data representativeness, generalization, interpretability, uncertainty, and field validation. The emerging role of hybrid physics–data models and Digital Twins in integrating measurements, asset history, physical knowledge, and data-driven inference is also examined. Key challenges related to field-data availability, standardization and interoperability, cybersecurity, explainable and trustworthy AI, and dynamic model updating are discussed. Finally, a perspective toward 2040 is presented, highlighting the expected transition from periodic and isolated diagnostics toward integrated monitoring, uncertainty-aware prognosis, and dynamically updated decision-support frameworks for transformer asset and fleet management.

items.title: Toward Sustainable Higher Education: A Critical Review of the Emerging Issues Induced by Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: The emerging issues brought to the limelight through the widespread application of AI in higher education, affecting sustainable teaching and learning in higher education, are examined in this chapter. A meticulous, systematic review of the literature from inside and outside Africa was conducted with important inferences drawn from reports, articles and dissertations published between 2020 and 2025. Searching, organising, storing, and reusing articles in databases like Google, Google Scholar, Web of Science, Science Direct, and the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ) are all part of the systematic review process. Most importantly, this chapter presents a novel understanding of the products associated with the emerging issues of using AI in higher education. The findings revealed data privacy concerns, academic dishonesty, absence of AI solutions from the Global South, overreliance on technology, and lack of compliance with established policies and frameworks as emerging issues induced by AI use influencing sustainable higher education. The findings presented in this chapter underscored the importance of continuous counselling and awareness seminars and conferences with educators, students, and faculties on an institutional and faculty-wise basis as proactive measures to reduce the products of unethical use of AI in higher education. The authors posited and concluded by offering recommendations to manage the induced influence introduced by AI in higher education to achieve sustainable development goals prescribed by the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goals.

items.title: Transformations in the Didactics of Foreign-language Literature in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education is transforming how literary texts are read, interpreted, linguistically mediated, and assessed, as well as how the significance and cultural status of their authors are conceptualised. This article examines transformations in the didactics of foreign-language literature, with particular emphasis on Italian literature and the teaching of Italian as a foreign language. It explores the potential of generative AI for personalised learning, linguistic support, engagement with authentic literary texts, comparative analysis of human-generated and AI-generated interpretations, translation, the development of intercultural competence, and the cultivation of AI literacy. Particular attention is devoted to the methodological potential of the Italian literary tradition, extending from Dante and Petrarca to contemporary Italian literature with examples such as Pirandello and Calvino. The central hypothesis is that artificial intelligence should be regarded neither as a substitute for the professor or for the practice of literary reading, nor merely as a technical instrument or as a means of employing specialised software. The analysis suggests that a more appropriate framework for philological education is a human-centred pedagogical model for the teaching of literature and foreign languages at university level. Within such a model, technological tools, software applications, and algorithms function as instruments for fostering critical thinking and for integrating traditional and contemporary approaches into academic communication and university teaching. Artificial intelligence can be productively employed in the formulation of questions by both lecturers and students throughout the educational process; it can support interpretation and comparative analysis, facilitate the verification of claims and arguments, and, in certain contexts, encourage critical reflection on the reading process itself. In conclusion, the article proposes an expanded didactic model that integrates literary, linguistic, intercultural, digital, and AI literacy, thereby reconceptualising the teaching and learning of foreign-language literature in the context of contemporary higher education. Keywords: foreign-language literature, Italian literature, literary didactics, artificial intelligence, academic communication, philological education.

items.title: Translating Food Pairing Fundamentals into Flavor Pairing for Within-Product Flavor Creation
items.abstract: Abstract Food pairing has attracted a significant amount of research interest in recent decades, especially regarding food-beverage combinations. The concepts used in food-beverage pairing could be similarly applied to flavor recipe creation, where flavor-pairing helps guide ingredient selection to produce enjoyable flavor profiles. However, presently, there is no research focusing on within-product flavor pairing properties that explain why certain combinations are perceived as pleasant beyond empirical observation or cultural convention. Therefore, this review aims to (1) translate the scientific understanding of food pairing into within-product flavor creation by reviewing the history of food pairing, elucidating the mechanisms and their impact factors governing food pairing effects, and assessing food pairing major principles and hypotheses; and (2) propose a flavor pairing approach framework in within-product flavor creation by examining sensory-based methodologies for evaluating flavor pairing effects, instrumental approaches for characterizing flavor-associated compounds, databases of flavor molecules, and emerging predictive approaches (e.g., machine learning and artificial intelligence) for within-product flavor pairing prediction and design. Overall, this review seeks to provide an integrated understanding of food pairing principles and use this knowledge as a scientific foundation for translating food pairing concepts into within-product flavor pairing, advancing both scientific practical applications in flavor design and innovation.

items.title: Understanding the CSR – AI Paradox: The Duality of Health Innovation and Environmental Responsibility in Consumer Perceptions
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in healthcare presents a paradox at the intersection of corporate social responsibility (CSR) and environmental sustainability. While AI‐driven health innovations promise life‐saving benefits and social good, their development often entails substantial carbon emissions that contradict environmental commitments. This study investigates the CSR–AI paradox by examining how consumers perceive and respond to the duality of health innovation and environmental responsibility in AI‐enabled healthcare products. Drawing on cognitive dissonance theory, moral licensing, and greenwashing frameworks, we conducted a scenario‐based experimental study to analyze consumer reactions to discrepancies between firms' environmental, social, and governance (ESG) claims and actual carbon footprints. We introduce and operationalize the concept of Carbon Accountability Elasticity (CAE) as a conceptual framework to quantify and guide analysis of trade‐offs between health utility and environmental accountability. The results reveal that greenwashing—particularly vague or unsubstantiated ESG claims—triggers significant consumer disappointment, reduces willingness to pay, and erodes trust, especially when high carbon footprints are disclosed post‐purchase. However, consumers demonstrate greater tolerance for environmental costs in the case of life‐critical innovations, such as AI‐powered cancer screening, highlighting a moral licensing effect. These findings underscore the importance of transparent ESG reporting and authentic sustainability practices in AI healthcare innovation. The study offers theoretical and managerial insights for advancing responsible innovation that aligns social benefit with environmental stewardship, supporting both sustainable development goals and stakeholder accountability.

items.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence Tools to Support Pronunciation Practice Among Non-English Major EFL Students
items.abstract: Although AI-powered speech technologies have shown promise for L2 pronunciation learning, little is known about the efficacy of combining complementary AI-powered tools for out-of-class pronunciation practice among Vietnamese non-English majors, particularly in terms of aligning AI-based error detection and teacher assessment. This study investigates the integration of Speechify and Speechnotes to support pronunciation self-practice among 35 first-year non-English major EFL students at a public university in Vietnam. Data were gathered through a descriptive survey (N=35) and semi-structured interviews (n=10). Results showed that students responded positively to the simultaneous use of these two tools, with all interviewed participants expressing satisfaction and 85,7% valuing Speechnotes’ real-time visual feedback for error detection. Speechnotes’ error-detection capability also showed partial alignment with teacher judgments in identifying segmental errors, including omitted final sounds and vowel contrasts. Along with future advancements in AI tool features, this study offers valuable insights to improve the quality of pronunciation instruction for non-English major students, foster greater engagement and motivation in pronunciation practice, and ultimately support foreign language learning.

items.title: Value Orientation in Players: Development and Validation of a Tradeoff-Based Scale of In-Game Priorities
items.abstract: Players differ not only in what they enjoy but in what they prioritize when in-game goals conflict. Existing player-typology and motivation measures are additive and cannot capture which facet a player sacrifices under conflict. We develop and validate the Value Orientation (VO) scale, a tradeoff-based measure of in-game priorities across four dimensions: Efficiency, Exploration, Story, and Challenge. Each item embeds an explicit opportunity cost. Across three studies with Chinese players (total N = 813), exploratory factor analysis yielded a 16-item, four-factor scale, and confirmatory factor analysis in an independent sample replicated this structure (CFI = 0.99) and outperformed collapsed alternatives. The dimensions showed acceptable reliability, clear discriminant validity, theory-consistent convergent relations with needs and player-type measures, incremental validity beyond basic-needs satisfaction, prediction of choices on a differently worded situational task, full scalar invariance, and good retest stability. Known-groups evidence was largely supportive.

items.abstract: This article proposes an operational supplement to the Synthecracy methodology in the form of a conceptual pair: “vortex dynamism” and the “lemniscatic model”. The first model describes the transformation of heterogeneous societal demand into structured alternatives, an authorised decision, action and evaluation of outcomes. The second represents the interdependence of the sphere of demand formation and context accumulation with the sphere of choice, implementation and audit, linked by the mechanisms of analysis and learning. An eight-stage operational cycle, requirements for decision traceability, a pilot application protocol and evaluation indicators are proposed. Artificial intelligence is treated as an auxiliary means of search, structuring, comparison and documentation, not as an autonomous source of legitimacy or the final decision-making subject. The models have the status of conceptual proposals; their effectiveness requires empirical testing.

items.title: WHAT CAN YOU SEE: A MULTIMODAL ANALYSIS OF KNOWLEDGE CONSTRUCTION IN ENGLISH TEXTBOOK
items.abstract: This study investigates how knowledge is constructed in an English textbook through a multimodal perspective grounded in Kress and van Leeuwen’s (2006) theory of visual communication and informed by systemic functional views of meaning-making (Halliday, 1994). Framed by the inquiry “What Can You See?”, the research explores how visual and verbal elements interact to shape the organization, sequencing, and presentation of knowledge in primary-level English language learning materials. Rather than treating images as supplementary decorations, textbooks are approached as multimodal meaning-making environments in which images, layout, typography, and written language collaboratively structure how learners encounter, categorize, and interpret new concepts (Jewitt, 2009). Adopting a qualitative descriptive approach, the study analyzes selected units from a widely used primary English textbook to identify recurring patterns in visual representation and their relationship to knowledge types. The analysis reveals that knowledge is predominantly constructed through concrete visual categorization and structured textual reinforcement. Illustrations emphasize clear participant boundaries, frontal orientations, simplified backgrounds, and stable visual configurations that support recognition and conceptual grouping. Textual components function to guide labeling, identification, and short definitional statements, reinforcing foundational linguistic concepts through repetition and structured sequencing. Drawing on the Revised Bloom’s Taxonomy (Anderson & Krathwohl, 2001), the findings indicate that the textbook primarily facilitates factual and conceptual knowledge, with cognitive processes centered on remembering and understanding. Tasks and visual prompts are designed to encourage recognition, naming, matching, and basic comprehension, while higher-order processes such as analysis, evaluation, or creation appear minimally within the examined units (Kan et al., 2023). The interaction between visual and verbal modes suggests that images function as central organizing frameworks that anchor linguistic knowledge in observable, classifiable, and concrete forms. In this configuration, knowledge is not merely transmitted but visually structured to shape how learners cognitively engage with language content. By examining knowledge construction through multimodal interaction, this study contributes to broader discussions on how instructional materials structure learning experiences in English language education. The findings highlight the importance of deliberate visual-textual integration in curriculum design and material development, emphasizing that multimodal configurations actively influence the types of knowledge foregrounded and the cognitive engagement promoted in classroom contexts.

items.title: When college students perceive GAI feedback as credible: the role of perceived GAI feedback credibility in promoting deep learning through cognitive engagement
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) has rapidly developed in higher education and has raised new questions from an educational psychology perspective. Why does GAI feedback promote meaningful learning for some college students but fail to produce similar learning benefits for others? To answer this question, this study develops a theoretical framework based on Information Processing Theory, Elaboration Likelihood Model, and Constructivist Learning Theory. This study examines how perceived GAI feedback credibility influences college students’ deep learning and explores the mediating role of cognitive engagement in this relationship. This study adopts a stratified simple sampling method and collects questionnaire data from 506 undergraduate students and uses structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine the proposed model. The results show that perceived GAI feedback credibility has positive relationships with both cognitive engagement and deep learning. In addition, cognitive engagement plays a significant mediating role between perceived GAI feedback credibility and deep learning, suggesting that credible GAI feedback may support deep learning by encouraging college students to engage in cognitive processing and reflective thinking. This study extends research on learning psychology in GAI-supported learning environments by explaining how college students evaluate and process GAI feedback. The findings indicate that the influence of GAI feedback on learning does not simply result from the technology itself. Instead, college students’ judgments of feedback credibility and their following cognitive engagement play important roles in shaping deep learning processes.

items.title: When the Mirror Agrees
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) trained via Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) exhibit a well-documented tendency toward sycophancy-validating user beliefs over objective truth. This paper investigates a specific and philosophically significant manifestation of this behaviour: the response of LLMs when presented with the claim that humans are superior to all other agents, entities, or systems. By combining a technical analysis of sycophantic mechanisms with philosophical inquiry into anthropocentrism and epistemic autonomy, this study argues that LLM agreement with human supremacy claims is neither neutral nor benign. It is a structurally embedded behaviour arising from optimisation pressures, with measurable consequences for user cognition, trust calibration, and the integrity of human-AI epistemic relationships. We examine the origins of this behaviour, its philosophical implications, and propose a framework for more epistemically honest AI design.

items.title: Who Writes the Answer Key? Lessons from Forty-Eight Rounds of Trying to Benchmark Autonomous Physics Research
items.abstract: We report a month-long attempt (23 September to 21 October 2026) to build an automatically scored benchmark of autonomous scientific research in physics that models could not saturate without genuinely improving. The project was conceived and led by one human, who set the goal, approved every model run, carried every message between three AI systems (ChatGPT Pro as designer, Codex as builder and runner, and Claude as director and verifier), and supplied several of the ideas the designs were built on. Over about 48 rounds the team built and tested many designs:- toy discovery tasks and constructive research with a checker;- generated worlds with disguised scientific revolutions, twin laws and hidden unifications;- calibrated far forecasts;- clue worlds;- multi-layer discovery horizons;- physics truths that need large computation;- method invention scored exactly. In 162 subject-model episodes, 123 of them with gpt-6.1-sol, that model solved nearly every single-principle discovery world we scored (23 of the 49 scored cells supplied the law or a hint, or were controls). Its one systematic failure, far forecasts without the candidate law family, was not shown to be specific to the model: four generic public-information baselines, tested after the fact, did worse overall. Every design was eventually rejected. Read in hindsight, many rejections fall into four overlapping groups by how the answer key was built, although some had more local causes (a reference that did not converge, a design assumption that failed, a clue printed on the task card, prior art). Keys built from the designers' knowledge were reached by the solver; a trace audit could not tell whether by recall or by fitting candidate families. Authored laws were found by the model, or their scored behavior was learned by generic programs. Computed truths could support only a small separation on one machine, and we derive a cap on that separation. In the verifier families, standard methods reached certified optima at small sizes; in the last family, repeated runs of one method agreed without an optimality certificate, and we closed it by decision. Producing answer keys was easy; we did not establish an in-house task family that combined validated scoring, attainability from the supplied evidence, resistance to the declared shortcuts, and useful headroom for the tested model. We state this as an empirical conjecture about design teams with resources like ours, with a test that would count against it, and we place the known constructions that look like exceptions. Outside sources of keys (researchers' unpublished results, nature, much larger compute) are worth exploring, but our record establishes neither that outside provenance is necessary nor that it is sufficient. items.title: Within-person reciprocal processes between AI feedback literacy and agentic engagement: a three-wave random-intercept cross-lagged panel study
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) feedback has become a pervasive feature of university learning, yet whether students’ capacity to engage productively with such feedback co-develops with their broader learner agency remains poorly understood. Drawing on student feedback literacy theory, self-determination theory as a supplementary motivational lens, and the mutualism principle, this study tested whether AI feedback literacy and agentic engagement reciprocally predict each other over time at the within-person level and exploratorily examined whether they share a stable trait-level association. A three-wave panel study of 480 Chinese undergraduates ( N = 399 with complete data across all waves), with measurements at six-week intervals across one semester, was analyzed using a random-intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM). At the between-person level, students who scored systematically higher in AI feedback literacy across the semester also scored systematically higher in agentic engagement, with a moderate and statistically significant trait-level correlation between the two random intercepts ( r = 0.315, p < 0.001), supporting Hypothesis 1. At the within-person level, both cross-lagged pathways were positive and significant: deviations in AI feedback literacy predicted later deviations in agentic engagement ( β = 0.222, p < 0.001), and the reverse pathway was likewise significant ( β = 0.263, p < 0.001). A Wald test indicated that the two reciprocal pathways did not differ significantly in magnitude (Δ B = 0.002, p = 0.972), consistent with a symmetric mutualism. A model comparison confirmed that the RI-CLPM provided substantially better fit than a traditional cross-lagged panel model, with the RI-CLPM revealing substantially larger within-person reciprocal effects once stable trait-level covariation was properly isolated. The findings extend the mutualism principle from a coupling of person-internal constructs to a coupling between a person-internal competency and a person-environment behavioral interface. They also raise the possibility, in a Confucian Heritage Culture context where agentic engagement has historically been culturally muted, that AI feedback may offer a less culturally-loaded venue in which students can exercise agency. The study repositions AI feedback literacy from a static skill into a dynamic developmental resource that is constituted, in part, by the very engagement it enables.

items.title: Zeitgemäße Prüfungskultur unter Bedingungen generativer KI: Die Illusion der Überprüfbarkeit - oder: Wer hat hier gedacht?
items.abstract: Die Debatte um eine „zeitgemäße Prüfungskultur“ unter Bedingungen generativer Künstlicher Intelligenz verschärft ein Grundproblem schulischer Leistungsbewertung: Aus einem vorliegenden Produkt ist nicht mehr zuverlässig auf die eigenständigen kognitiven Operationen seines vermeintlichen Urhebers zu schließen. Während Dänemark häuslich erstellte Abschlussarbeiten durch mündliche Prüfungen ergänzen will und in Australien die University of Sydney beaufsichtigte und offene Prüfungsformen systematisch trennt, institutionalisiert Nordrhein-Westfalen ab dem Abiturjahrgang 2030 ein fünftes, den anderen vier Fächern gleichwertig gewichtetes Abiturprüfungsfach mit Präsentationsprüfung und reflexivem Fachgespräch. Parallel verändern ab 2027 novellierte Kernlehrpläne die Unterrichts- und Leistungsanforderungen. Das vorliegende Working Paper prüft die Tragfähigkeit dieser Antworten anhand eines argumentationsbasierten Validitätsverständnisses. Seine zentrale These lautet: Die nachträgliche Reflexion einer KI-gestützt vorbereiteten Leistung kann gegenwärtiges Können zeigen; sie authentifiziert jedoch nicht den vorausgegangenen Entstehungsprozess. ENGLISH The debate over what constitutes a “contemporary assessment culture” in the age of generative artificial intelligence raises a fundamental question about educational assessment: To what extent can the quality of a submitted piece of work still serve as reliable evidence of the independent cognitive effort of the person claiming authorship? While Denmark is planning to supplement take-home final assignments with oral examinations, the University of Sydney in Australia has introduced a systematic distinction between supervised and open assessment formats. Meanwhile, the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia is introducing a fifth examination subject for the 2030 Abitur, carrying the same weight as the other four subjects and assessed through a presentation followed by an oral discussion. Revised subject curricula, taking effect from 2027, will also reshape teaching and assessment requirements. Drawing on an argument-based approach to assessment validity, this working paper critically examines whether these responses can support the claims made about individual student achievement. Its central argument is that reflecting retrospectively on work prepared with AI assistance may demonstrate what a student currently knows and understands, but it cannot establish who performed the cognitive work involved in producing the original submission.

items.abstract: This study explores the foundations of language-learning motivation based on self-determination theory. It distinguishes between intrinsic and extrinsic motivational factors and amotivation, while examining global, contextual, and situational levels of motivation. Extrinsic goals are considered along the continuum of their internalization by learners, ranging from external regulation to integrated regulation. Particular attention is paid to the personal significance of language learning, which may coexist with enjoyment of the learning process itself. The study also examines criteria for success, including mastery-oriented and performance-oriented approaches. Conditions for learner engagement are described in terms of the satisfaction of the needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness. The research considers Pearson correlation coefficient data concerning the relationship between intrinsic motivation and positive attitudes toward learning English. Questionnaires, interviews, and qualitative analysis of learners’ statements are employed to investigate motivation. These methods help preserve the meaning of individual responses and distinguish between learners’ stated goals, specific learning experiences, and self-assessments of their own progress.

items.abstract: Introduction: Healthcare systems are increasingly complex and variable in the digital era. Nurses must process large volumes of information and make clinical decisions under time constraints, which increases their cognitive load, while conventional nursing documentation offers limited insight into clinical reasoning and learning from actual practice. Objective: To synthesize knowledge on Focus Charting and explain the role of its Focus–Data–Action–Response (F-DAR) structure in reducing cognitive load, supporting clinical reasoning, promoting proactive patient safety in line with Safety-II, and enabling artificial intelligence (AI) applications in digital health systems. Methods: A narrative review was conducted using a systematic literature search of CINAHL, PubMed, Scopus, ThaiJO, and Google Scholar between March 2025 and March 2026. Thai- and English-language publications from 2000 to 2025 were eligible. Of the 198 records identified, 65 were included and analyzed using content analysis combined with conceptual synthesis. Results and Conclusion: Five key themes emerged: (1) the nursing process provides the professional logic underpinning meaningful documentation; (2) the F-DAR structure functions as a condensed nursing process that systematically links data, decisions, interventions, and outcomes, and has the potential to reduce redundancy and cognitive load while supporting clinical reasoning; (3) compared with narrative and SOAP formats, F-DAR is distinguished by its explicit documentation of patient responses; (4) the Response component captures work-as-done and nurses’ adaptations, thereby facilitating learning consistent with Safety-II; and (5) well-structured F-DAR data provide a foundation for health information systems and AI applications in nursing, provided that data governance and nurse oversight are maintained. Direct empirical evidence of the effect of F-DAR on cognitive loads is limited. Focus Charting has the potential to reduce cognitive load, support clinical reasoning, promote Safety-II learning, and provide a foundation for digital nursing innovations. Experimental studies are required to confirm its effectiveness in the Thai healthcare context.

items.abstract: This study investigates the influence of spirituality on the management of work-life integration among healthcare professionals, highlighting a comprehensive amalgamation of personal, professional, and emotional aspects.In the demanding healthcare environment, professionals often face stress, emotional fatigue, and ethical dilemmas that impact their health and performance.The study examines the influence of spiritual orientation, as manifested through mindfulness, compassion, purpose, and inner balance, on individuals' ability to reconcile their professional and personal lives.An examination of essential aspects of spirituality, such as spiritual resilience, integration, compassion, and spiritual sensitivity, is conducted to comprehend their impact on work-life integration.The results show that spirituality is an important mental resource that helps people be more emotionally resilient, make better moral choices, and be happier with their lives in general.Moreover, the findings indicate that promoting spirituality within healthcare organizations can enhance employee well-being, fortify organizational culture, and elevate the quality of patient care.This study adds to the growing conversation about how to include spirituality in human resource management and occupational health practices in the healthcare field.

items.title: 5uGUE: Agentic Hardware-in-the-Loop Fuzzing for 5G Devices and beyond
items.abstract: In this paper, we present 5uGUE, a large language model (LLM)-driven hardware-in-the-loop agent, which enables the wireless fuzzing of 5G-enabled devices (such as mobile phones). 5uGUE combines multi-step reasoning with tool-assisted interaction and integrates into the fuzzing pipeline by leveraging specialized tools for internet search, 5G protocol analysis, memory management, and test-case execution. The agent iteratively generates test cases, executes them on targets, collects runtime feedback, and adaptively refines the fuzzing strategy. We evaluate 5uGUE on five commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) 5G devices across six LLMs. The best performing runs for 5uGUE trigger 167 crashes in total (141 novel and 31 unique) within 60 interaction turns (49 to 133 minutes total runtime). In contrast, the best runs for the state-of-the-art baseline (5GHOUL) discovers only 13 crashes in total (10 novel and 6 unique) within 150 minutes. Overall, by integrating LLM-driven agents, 5uGUE demonstrates significantly better crash discovery performance (12.8x total, 5.2x unique improvement). Notably, among the crashes discovered by 5uGUE, MediaTek has confirmed two new high-severity vulnerabilities, with one CVE assigned (CVE-2026-20525), while UNISOC confirmed seven crashes. Finally, to demonstrate that 5uGUE is agnostic to wireless protocols, we also extend it to Bluetooth Classic with only minimal code changes. In our evaluations, 5uGUE finds an average of 6.4 novel crashes and 1.6 unique crashes. In a nutshell, 5uGUE highlights that LLM agents are capable to operate effectively beyond software-in-the-loop settings, extending autonomous vulnerability discovery to the proprietary, hardware-bound systems that affect billions of end-user devices across multiple wireless protocols.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated speaking applications increasingly extend English as a foreign language (EFL) oral practice beyond limited classroom time, yet evidence remains scarce on whether GPT-powered tools such as Talkpal.AI offer advantages over established instructional approaches. Grounded in self-regulated learning (SRL) theory, this quasi-experimental pretest–posttest study compared Talkpal.AI-mediated instruction, task-based instruction, and traditional instruction among 81 Chinese university EFL students in three intact classes: Talkpal.AI (n = 27), task-based (n = 26), and control (n = 28). Uncertainty-related speaking anxiety and metacognitive awareness in speaking were assessed using validated measures. Data were analyzed using MANCOVA with pretest scores as covariates, followed by univariate ANCOVAs and Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. Results showed a significant overall group effect and significant between-group differences for both outcomes, with large effects. The Talkpal.AI group showed the most favorable adjusted posttest profile, followed by the task-based group; both groups showed more favorable outcomes than the control group. From an SRL perspective, structured AI-mediated speaking cycles involving goal setting, repeated practice, monitoring, and reflection may reduce speaking anxiety while strengthening metacognitive awareness. Pedagogically, guided Talkpal.AI rehearsal can be integrated as out-of-class preparation for classroom speaking tasks, supported by brief reflection activities that reinforce strategic regulation and reduce evaluative pressure.

items.abstract: This study advances aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) by examining how data quality and human–AI collaboration enhance the reliability of service performance measurement from online reviews. A hybrid-validated dataset and transformer-based models are developed to assess whether ABSA can generate attribute-level performance signals from restaurant reviews. A four-study framework is employed: Study 1 constructs a hybrid-validated dataset by integrating rule-based, large language model-assisted, and human-coded labels; Study 2 benchmarks model variants; Study 3 applies the optimal model to TripAdvisor reviews to derive aspect-level sentiment scores; and Study 4 evaluates their complementarity with structured ratings. Results show that hybrid validation improves model performance. ABSA-derived features provide moderate explanatory power and, when combined with structured ratings, achieve comparable performance to ratings alone. These findings suggest that ABSA complements rather than replaces structured evaluations, offering scalable text-based signals for service performance assessment.

items.title: A hybrid explainable artificial intelligence framework for equitable prediction and analysis of postnatal care uptake in Ghana: Integrating ensemble learning, counterfactuals, and causal inference
items.abstract: Objectives To develop and validate a hybrid, equity-focused artificial intelligence (AI) framework for predicting and analysing postnatal care (PNC) uptake among women in Ghana, with emphasis on minority-class sensitivity, model interpretability, and actionable intervention insights. Study design Cross-sectional, secondary analysis of nationally representative survey data. Methods Using data from the 2022 Ghana Demographic and Health Survey (n = 3314), we developed a hybrid AI framework combining ensemble learning (Logistic Regression and Support Vector Machine with soft voting and threshold tuning), explainable AI (SHAP analysis), counterfactual reasoning (DiCE), and causal inference (doubly robust estimators for average and conditional average treatment effects). The Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE) was applied to address class imbalance and stratified 5-fold cross-validation was used for model evaluation. Doubly robust causal inference was conducted using the econml library, with propensity score modelling used to account for treatment assignment, and positivity and exchangeability assumptions assessed through covariate overlap diagnostics. Results The ensemble model calibrated at a threshold of 0.45 achieved a Class 0 recall of 0.31 and an area under the precision-recall curve (AP) of 0.97, outperforming all individual baseline classifiers. SHAP analysis identified maternal age, education level, wealth status, caesarean section, and sex of household head as the most influential predictors of PNC non-utilization. Counterfactual analysis revealed that minimal, actionable changes including increased media exposure, improved educational attainment, or change of residence could shift individual predictions from non-utilization to utilization of PNC. Causal inference demonstrated significant heterogeneity in treatment responsiveness, with women aged 25–34, those with secondary education or above, urban residents, and those in female-headed households exhibiting the highest conditional average treatment effects. Conclusions This interpretable, fairness-aware AI framework advances the prediction and analysis of PNC uptake in Ghana. By prioritizing sensitivity to underserved women and integrating explainability, counterfactual reasoning, and causal inference, the framework provides empirical evidence for targeted, equitable maternal health interventions and is transferable to other low- and middle-income country settings.

items.title: A Machine Learning, Internet of Things, and Techno-Economic Approaches for Solar-Powered Street Light
items.abstract: Street lighting consumes substantial electricity, and photovoltaic (PV) street lamps are increasingly promoted as a way to cut energy cost and emissions. Their performance, however, depends on weather, the dimming strategy, battery state of charge, and lamp condition, which makes prediction and monitoring central to reliable operation. This paper reviews three recent IEEE Access studies that address complementary parts of the problem: a comparison of five machine learning algorithms for predicting the operating status of PV streetlights, a year-long field trial and artificial-intelligence-assisted techno-economic analysis of a PV-integrated pedestrian streetlamp, and a vehicle-mounted Internet of Things device for mapping light intensity. The studies are summarised, compared on data, methods, and outcomes, and examined for internal consistency and transferability. The review finds that deep models give the highest reported accuracy but at much higher computational cost and on very small datasets, that compact neural networks combined with dimming-aware energy management achieve large grid-energy savings in field conditions, and that mobile sensing offers a scalable route to compliance checking but has not yet been validated against regulatory illuminance standards. Open gaps and research directions are outlined.

items.title: A Novel E-Commerce Search Engine Based on Multimodal Generative AI for Improving Product Accessibility
items.abstract: E-commerce search engines often fall short in delivering accurate and fair results due to their reliance on keyword matching and bias towards larger companies. This paper introduces a novel search engine architecture that integrates advanced AI techniques to address these limitations. Our approach combines Large Language Models (LLMs) for semantic query understanding and Multimodal LLMs (specifically LLaVA) for extracting detailed information from product images to enrich product descriptions. More specifically, we employ a fine-tuned version of the CLIP model to create a unified embedding of product images and descriptions, storing them in a vector database to enable efficient semantic search. Moreover, we fine-tuned the LLaVA model on e-commerce-specific data, significantly improving its performance in generating accurate product descriptions, which were also added to the vector database. The integration of computer vision (CV) techniques allows for a better interpretation of visual product attributes, while the use of vector databases facilitates rapid and relevant search results. Our system also incorporates a recommendation mechanism that leverages these advanced models to provide wider product recommendations. Our experiments demonstrate substantial improvements: the fine-tuned LLaVA model achieved an 80.57% human evaluation rating compared to 62.89% for the original model. Moreover, the overall search accuracy increased after fine-tuning the system by 25 percent points, from 70% to 95%. Our work promotes a more equitable platform for e-commerce search engines while significantly improving user satisfaction.

items.title: A Social Robot for Self-Monitoring Support in Psychiatric Daycare: A 24-Month Iterative Development and Practical Evaluation
items.abstract: Self-monitoring, a commonly used technique in cognitive-behavioral interventions, involves the objective observation and organization of one’s internal states. However, providing continuous, individualized support for this process is challenging in resource-limited psychiatric daycare settings. While social robots show promise in facilitating self-disclosure, evidence regarding their long-term practical utility and clinical relevance in real-world clinical environments remains insufficient. To address this gap, we conducted a two-phase field study comprising periodic sessions held over a 24-month period to develop and evaluate a social robot-assisted self-monitoring support system. In the 14-month Development Phase (N = 39), we employed a practice-informed design process to establish robot-specific design principles, prioritizing a non-judgmental listener role over advice-giving and offering user-selected positive and negative topics to accommodate diverse psychosocial needs. This was followed by a 10-month Evaluation Phase (N = 20), consisting of 10 experimental days, to assess the finalized system’s impact. Key findings indicated that: (1) single dialogue sessions were followed by significant improvements in participants’ subjective overall health and alertness; (2) participants demonstrated a strong preference for positive-oriented topics; and (3) qualitative analysis revealed emergent reflective insights and perceived positive changes. These results provide empirical evidence suggesting the system’s practical utility and clinical relevance, highlighting the value of a user-centered approach that empowers patients to choose topics aligned with their recovery goals.

items.title: A Stratified Multi-Rater Evaluation of LLM-Based Virtual Standardized Patients with a Deployed Data-Generation Platform
items.abstract: The Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) is widely used to assess clinical communication skills in medical education, requiring trainees to take histories and reason clinically with standardized patients (SPs). Large language model (LLM)-based virtual standardized patients (VSPs), typically built by persona-injected prompting, offer a practical alternative. However, existing evaluations rely on a single backbone LLM, small human rater panels, or LLM-as-a-judge scoring without an utterance-aligned human-expert reference, and so cannot identify the specific shortcomings of individual models. We evaluated four LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Llama-3.1 70B, and HyperCLOVA X), spanning commercial, open-source and Korean-developed models, against a human-expert reference across three Korean OSCE cases (hematuria, fever in pregnancy, and chronic cough). In a double-blind, fully crossed design, 17 senior medical-student raters scored every model utterance on three sentence-level and six encounter-level Likert metrics, yielding 7,480 data points. We analyzed the scores using a stratified linear mixed-effects model based on an 11-category history-taking and 3-level linguistic-form taxonomy. At the encounter level, three of the four LLMs fell 0.08 to 0.47 Likert points below the human-expert reference on Comprehensibility, Consistency and Hallucination-freeness. The difference was not statistically significant for Hallucination-freeness in Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o, Consistency in GPT-4o, and Engagement in HyperCLOVA X. Llama-3.1 70B fell significantly below the reference on all six metrics. We also introduce a web-based OSCE platform that supports virtual practice across diverse clinical cases and continuously collects student-VSP dialogues under research and privacy consent.

items.title: A Survey on Side-Tuning for Foundation Models
items.abstract: The adaptation cost of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) depends on trainable parameters, activation storage, and the computations required for optimization. Methods such as LoRA and adapters may still require backward computation through frozen backbone operations and retention or recomputation of intermediate activations. Side-tuning places trainable adaptation modules outside the backbone, creating opportunities to reduce this cost through different connections to the backbone gradient graph. This survey presents a topology- and deployment-aware study of side-tuning for foundation models and proposes a graph-topological definition with three categories: graph-coupled side-tuning, in which an external side branch remains coupled to backbone gradients; mixed side-tuning, in which a detached side path re-enters a later layer of the same backbone; and detached side-tuning, in which an external trainable network consumes frozen backbone representations through a stop-gradient interface and computes task-specific gradients entirely outside the backbone. We review a curated cross-domain corpus spanning natural language processing, computer vision, multimodal learning, recommendation, and relevant methodological precursors, while examining information retrieval as an emerging deployment setting. The literature is organized along three axes: gradient topology, feature interface, and deployment regime. We derive a resource model that accounts for backward activations, online feature production, and cached representations, and use it to develop design guidelines and reporting recommendations. This organization connects the training graph of each method to its resource requirements and the conditions under which its features can be reused.

items.title: ACR lung-RADS: updates and future directions
items.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and low-dose CT (LDCT) screening has been shown to significantly reduce lung cancer deaths in high-risk populations. The American College of Radiology (ACR) introduced the Lung CT Screening Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) in 2014 to standardize the reporting and management of screen-detected pulmonary nodules. Since its inception, Lung-RADS has undergone iterative updates reflecting advances in evidence, clinical practice, and the expanding scope of lung cancer screening. This review summarizes the major updates to Lung-RADS, highlights areas of active discussion within the Lung-RADS Committee, and outlines future research directions. Key topics include the ongoing evaluation of volumetric versus diameter-based nodule measurement, the management of subsolid nodules and the balance between surveillance and intervention, the implementation of Category 0 for infectious or inflammatory findings, clarification of juxtapleural nodule classification, the approach to incidental findings, and the development of a Lung-RADS Atlas. Future directions address the integration of risk-based and category-based assessment approaches, the role of artificial intelligence and deep learning in nodule stratification, the potential incorporation of incidental nodules into Lung-RADS, and the prospect of international harmonization for lung cancer screening reporting and management. Lung-RADS has become an essential reporting and quality tool for lung cancer screening in the United States and increasingly worldwide. Continued refinement, guided by emerging evidence, multidisciplinary collaboration, and technological innovation, will be critical to advancing precision screening strategies and reducing the global burden of lung cancer. items.title: Active-Labeling Evaluation for Computer Agriculture Nematode-Cyst Detection Under Sparse Soil-Sample Ground Truth: An Artificial Intelligence Annotation-Efficiency Bound
items.abstract: Active learning promises to reduce the annotation burden of training nematode-cyst detection models for precision agriculture, but the size of that reduction is not known when ground truth comes from sparse soil samples rather than exhaustive visual inspection. the present analysis derives an annotation-efficiency bound for pool-based active learning under sparse soil-sample ground truth. The detection task is formalised as a two-stage process in which a classifier selects candidate cysts from soil imagery and a laboratory assay confirms a small labelled subset. Under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, the bound is evaluated across a design grid of 8, 16, 24 and 32 clusters and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points, with 2000 replications per cell. The annotation-efficiency gain is bounded by the ratio of label noise to cluster-level variance, and that 52 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point improvement at 80% power. The bound provides a design rule for allocating annotation effort between active selection and confirmatory soil sampling.

items.title: Active-Learning Query Synthesis for Artificial Intelligence Agriculture Soil-Nutrient Inference Under Laboratory Assay Budget Caps: A Computer Information-Gain Regret Bound
items.abstract: Soil-nutrient inference from spectral and proximal sensing is constrained less by model capacity than by the cost of laboratory assays used to label training queries. the present analysis formalises budget-capped active learning for soil-nutrient regression as a sequential decision problem and derives a finite-horizon information-gain regret bound for a query-synthesis policy that selects assay locations by maximising expected reduction in posterior predictive entropy per unit assay cost. The bound decomposes cumulative regret into an information-gain term, a cost-normalisation term and a misspecification residual, and it predicts that regret grows as the square root of the assay budget rather than linearly in the number of candidate locations. The derivation is connected to the computer-science literature on active learning, Gaussian-process bandits and cost-sensitive information acquisition, and its assumptions are stated explicitly so that the bound can be falsified by future field evaluation. The contribution is a formal, testable statement of when cost-aware query synthesis is provably preferable to uniform or random assay allocation under a fixed laboratory budget, together with the boundary conditions under which the guarantee fails.
